title: A strategy for feasible water-main instances

blocks.text: The water utility's property tests (practice 1) need instances to run on, and a random instance is often useless: a must-do that costs more than the budget makes the whole instance infeasible, and then there is no plan to check. Write a Hypothesis strategy whose every instance has a valid plan.
The rules are the selection's of practice 1: with $`y_p \in \{0,1\}`$,
Write `instances()` in `water_strategy.py`, a `@st.composite` strategy returning the dict described in its docstring, with project names of your choice. Each instance must have:

items: one to six projects, and every project a key of `cost`, `needs` and `value`;
capital costs of 1 to 40, operating costs of 1 to 10, and values of 1 to 20;
at most two prerequisites per project, each another project, and no chain of prerequisites that leads back to where it started;
must-dos, and budgets, such that some plan meets all four rules;
budgets that are sometimes tight: across the drawn instances, funding every project at once must sometimes break a budget.

blocks.text: The tests draw 150 instances with a fixed seed and check each condition. About fifteen lines.

"""A Hypothesis strategy for water-main selection instances that always have a valid plan.

An instance is a dict:
    "cost":   {project: (capital $k, operating $k)}
    "budget": (capital budget $k, operating budget $k)
    "must":   [projects that must be funded]
    "needs":  {project: [its prerequisites]}, every project a key
    "value":  {project: value}
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from hypothesis import strategies as st


@st.composite
def instances(draw) -> dict:
    names = [f"w{k}" for k in range(1, draw(st.integers(1, 6)) + 1)]
    cost, needs, value, chosen = {}, {}, {}, set()
    for k, name in enumerate(names):
        cost[name] = (draw(st.integers(1, 40)), draw(st.integers(1, 10)))
        value[name] = draw(st.integers(1, 20))
        earlier = names[:k]
        needs[name] = draw(st.lists(st.sampled_from(earlier), unique=True, max_size=2)) if earlier else []
        if all(q in chosen for q in needs[name]) and draw(st.booleans()):
            chosen.add(name)
    must = [p for p in names if p in chosen and draw(st.booleans())]
    capital = sum(cost[p][0] for p in chosen) + draw(st.integers(0, 30))
    operating = sum(cost[p][1] for p in chosen) + draw(st.integers(0, 8))
    return {"cost": cost, "budget": (capital, operating), "must": must, "needs": needs, "value": value}


if __name__ == "__main__":
    print(instances().example())

cases.says: every drawn instance has one to six projects, the five fields, and prerequisites that are other existing projects
a must-do's prerequisites must be paid for too, so every drawn instance has a plan that meets all four rules
no project is its own prerequisite through a chain, so prerequisites point only one way
the budgets are tight enough that funding every project breaks one of them in some draws
